title: Modular private deployment pricing: license vs support subscription + upgrade cadence experiment
creator: Lena Morales
description:
Run a controlled experiment to validate a modular commercial offering for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that separates: (A) an upfront perpetual (or multi-year) license fee for the software, (B) a recurring support & updates subscription with tiered SLAs, and (C) optional accelerated upgrade windows. Goal: find a packaging that 1) increases NRR vs our current bundled approach, 2) reduces negotiation friction during SOC2/KMS/Airgap discussions, and 3) yields predictable revenue for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope: enterprise customers evaluating Private or VPC deployments; exclude Hosted API renewals. Deliverables: pricing matrix, contract amendment template, pilot offer letter, telemetry instrumentation plan, and recommended default for sales reps.

Hypotheses: 1) Offering a lower upfront license + paid annual support will increase conversion of POCs to paid pilots. 2) An optional 30/90/180-day upgrade SLA (paid) will capture ~10-15% of early adopters who require strict maintenance windows. 3) Separating license from support reduces legal lead time for customers that need custom KMS/HSM terms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pricing matrix with at least 3 discrete commercial offers (Basic/Business/Enterprise) including list price ranges and expected discount bands.
- Contract amendment (word doc) incorporating license fee, support tiers, and upgrade cadence annex drafted and approved by Legal.
- Security questionnaire doc updated with standard responses for support tiers and upgrade policies.
- Instrumentation defined and implemented: conversion, time-to-sign, ARR impact, churn by cohort.
- Pilot with 3 signed customers running by 2025-03-20 and initial telemetry collected.
comments: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting with Sales, Legal, Security. Agreed to run modular packaging as a 6-week experiment targeting inbound Private leads. Action: Sales to nominate 6 candidate accounts for outreach (Jonas).

2025-02-18: Sales interviews completed (6 accounts). Common asks: stricter upgrade windows, explicit KMS/HSM ownership language, and clear support SLA credits. Two accounts flagged as high-priority (healthcare and fintech).

2025-02-21: Legal provided initial clause language for license fee vs subscription separation. Flag: need to align refund/termination language for prepaid multi-year licenses. Legal suggests a reserved-escrow clause for air-gapped customers. (Link: https://confluence.redwood.company/private-packaging/clauses)

2025-02-24: Security (Nadia Singh) reviewed questionnaire. Items added: offline upgrade attestations, KMS integration matrix, patch timeline commitments per support tier. Security requested an FAQ for customers about responsibility boundaries. Asked to include SOC2/AICPA language in amendment.

2025-02-27: Pricing PM prototype completed. Three tier sketches: Silver (license + annual basic support, 48-72 hr patch SLA), Gold (license + prioritized support, 30-day upgrade window), Platinum (license + 24/7 support + paid accelerated upgrade windows: 30/90-day). Built modeled ARR and CAC assumptions for each. Initial recommendation: price Gold ~20% above Silver, Platinum +40% vs Silver.

2025-02-28: Engineering estimate (Ravi Patel): additional operational cost per accelerated upgrade window ~0.8 FTE equivalent during release periods for first 6 months, thereafter amortized. Need to quantify runbook and automation scope.

2025-03-03: Draft contract amendment uploaded to Drive (link: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/private-pricing-pilot). Legal review scheduled for 2025-03-05. Sales enablement doc draft created for pilot messaging.

2025-03-04: Pilot cohort selected (3 customers): Acme Health, BlueLedger Finance, Nimbus Retail. Each agreed to pilot terms with variation on upgrade cadence. Next: finalize instrumented offer flow in Stripe/contract system and onboard customer success to capture feedback.
